resources.title: Choose a tool by the question you have

paragraphs.text: Use the worksheet when you have one headline, product statement or paper to inspect. Write your question before you start reading, then keep a separate space for the source’s actual scope. For example, the FOPH wearable fact sheet distinguishes a watch connected through a phone from a watch using a mobile network directly. A note that says only smartwatch exposure loses that distinction. Record the connection arrangement before deciding whether the source addresses your question.
paragraphs.locator: PDF introduction and section 1, physical pages 1 and 2

paragraphs.text: Use the reading guide when you need to compare unlike records. A technical explanation, an exposure measurement and a study of illness contribute different information. NCI’s fact sheet first explains field quantities and common sources, then discusses cancer research separately. Follow that separation in your own notes: identify what the source describes before treating it as evidence for a health conclusion. The guide and worksheet organize that process; they do not perform an individual exposure assessment.
paragraphs.locator: HTML: What are electric and magnetic fields?; What are common sources of non-ionizing EMFs?

paragraphs.text: Try the ICNIRP cordless-phone record as a short example. Identify the base station and portable handset as separate parts of the setup. The source describes far-field exposure relative to the base station and near-field exposure relative to a handset or monitor. In the worksheet, put those descriptions under exposure, rather than entering one value for the entire system. Under comparison, write which part of the setup a second source actually measured.
paragraphs.locator: HTML: Characteristics of the application and its use

paragraphs.text: Then write one limit on the interpretation. The cordless-phone page says much of the health discussion draws on mobile-phone and base-station literature. That makes the origin of the evidence relevant: a discussion on a DECT application page is not automatically a new DECT-specific experiment. Keep the source type and the tested technology visible. Open the original source whenever you need its complete wording, references or technical conditions.
paragraphs.locator: HTML: HF effects on the body and health implications

paragraphs.text: Keep the notes tied to one reading session. Save the document title, the passage you inspected and the date you accessed it. The same technical source may be useful for identifying an exposure while leaving a health question unanswered. That is a reason to specify the next source needed, rather than stretching the original source into a broader verdict.
paragraphs.locator: HTML: What are electric and magnetic fields?; What have studies shown about possible associations between non-ionizing EMFs and cancer in children?

fields.title: Start with the field, then the exposure

paragraphs.text: A source name is a starting point for classification, not a complete exposure description. NCI distinguishes static fields, fields associated with electrical power systems and radiofrequency sources. Its examples include household wiring and appliances in the low-frequency group, and wireless communication devices in the radiofrequency group. The categories below help you reach the relevant reading pages. They do not assign one health verdict to every device or every situation within a category.
paragraphs.locator: HTML: What are electric and magnetic fields?; What are common sources of non-ionizing EMFs?

paragraphs.text: Static magnetic fields do not vary with time. ICNIRP’s static-field explanation uses the Earth’s field, magnets and specialized equipment as examples. This is a different starting point from an alternating field. Its protection discussion also distinguishes general static-field exposure, movement through strong fields and MRI procedures. When reading an equipment description, check which of those situations is actually addressed instead of transferring advice between them.
paragraphs.locator: HTML: Characteristics of the field and its use; Protection

fields.title: Keep the quantity and comparison visible

paragraphs.text: An electric-field reading and a magnetic-field reading are different quantities. NCI explains electric fields in relation to voltage and magnetic fields in relation to current, and describes their units separately. A comparison therefore needs the measured quantity as well as the number. Record frequency, position, operating conditions and duration where reported. If a paper supplies only a device-use questionnaire, keep that exposure measure rather than replacing it with a field measurement that was never made.
paragraphs.locator: HTML: What are electric and magnetic fields?

paragraphs.text: A wireless system can contain more than one relevant source. ICNIRP describes the base station and nearby handset separately for DECT. Use the source-specific pages when a broad field label is insufficient. A category identifies where to look next; the actual device, body position, exposure conditions and endpoint determine how closely a study matches a question.
paragraphs.locator: HTML: Characteristics of the application and its use

paragraphs.text: Read guidance and research as distinct kinds of information. The static-field page describes protection against established effects and separate issues for implanted devices. It does not turn every listed source into an individual risk calculation. Likewise, finding an exposure category here is not a compliance check on your equipment. Follow the original document for its scope and technical conditions, and keep unresolved source or setting differences explicit.
paragraphs.locator: HTML: Protection

reading-worksheet.title: Work through one example before comparing studies

paragraphs.text: Begin with a precise question such as whether a source measured the same wearable connection you are asking about. The FOPH fact sheet describes both communication through a paired phone and direct mobile-network communication. Write the tested arrangement, not just the product category. If your question concerns a different mode or device, record the mismatch before copying the source’s conclusion. This keeps the note useful even when it cannot answer your original question.
paragraphs.locator: PDF introduction and section 1, physical pages 1 and 2

paragraphs.text: Next, distinguish the measurement from an outcome. FOPH describes tests using models of body parts, called phantoms, under specified operating conditions. Such a measurement concerns exposure in the tested setup. It is not a follow-up of people developing a disease. Put the measurement method in its own field and leave a clinical-outcome field unfilled when the document does not provide one. Do not convert a laboratory measurement into a personal diagnosis.
paragraphs.locator: PDF section 2.4, physical pages 4 and 5

reading-worksheet.title: Make the final two sentences specific

paragraphs.text: For the cordless-phone example, a useful first sentence is that the source explains the base station and portable handset as different exposure situations. A useful second sentence is that this description does not tell you the exposure of a particular room or person. ICNIRP’s application page supplies the distinction; your actual room, device activity and position still need their own information. Link the passage so another reader can see why you kept those questions separate.
paragraphs.locator: HTML: Characteristics of the application and its use

paragraphs.text: Keep source access separate from certainty. NCI’s fact sheet links to research about several different cancer questions; the presence of a reference does not mean you inspected that paper’s methods. In the worksheet, label whether you read the fact sheet, an abstract or the full paper. Record the relevant section beside the claim you paraphrased. A clear source trail helps the next reader check the reasoning without assuming that every cited study was independently appraised.
paragraphs.locator: HTML: What have studies shown about possible associations between non-ionizing EMFs and cancer in children?

reading-guide.title: What the reading method looks like

paragraphs.text: First name the physical situation. NCI places wiring, power lines and household appliances in the low-frequency discussion and wireless communication equipment in the radiofrequency discussion. A paper about one group should not silently become an answer about another. Write the source and exposure measure beside your question, then check whether the population, comparison and outcome also match. Use the linked original document when the short description here is not enough.
paragraphs.locator: HTML: What are common sources of non-ionizing EMFs?

paragraphs.text: Then ask what kind of evidence the document supplies. FOPH’s wearable fact sheet includes a measurement discussion using selected devices and body-part models. It explicitly says the measurements are not a market overview. That is a useful example of a bounded finding: it can describe tested arrangements without certifying every watch or fitness tracker. Reading the sample and test conditions is part of interpreting the result, rather than an optional detail after the headline.
paragraphs.locator: PDF section 2.4, physical pages 4 and 5

paragraphs.text: Finally keep the limit beside the conclusion. ICNIRP’s static-field page discusses general protection, movement through strong fields, MRI procedures and implanted devices as distinct issues. A short general explanation cannot replace those different assessments. In your summary, say which issue the source addresses and which remains unanswered. This edition teaches that source-reading process. It does not supply a new clinical recommendation, a device certificate or an independently completed appraisal of the literature.
paragraphs.locator: HTML: Protection

first-guide-preview.title: Try the method on a technical source

paragraphs.text: The FOPH wearable fact sheet provides a practical example of why the exposure description belongs beside the conclusion. It distinguishes communication through a paired phone or wireless router from direct mobile-network communication. In a reading note, name that connection path before comparing a finding with a different device. The word wearable alone does not preserve the tested arrangement. This is an exercise in matching the question to the source, rather than choosing a product.
paragraphs.locator: PDF introduction and section 1, physical pages 1 and 2

paragraphs.text: The same fact sheet says its measurement sample is not a market overview. It describes tests on selected devices using phantoms that represent exposed body parts. A summary should retain that sample limit and measurement setting. It should not become a claim that all models were tested or that a measurement establishes a long-term health outcome. Keep the original document linked and note the page containing the condition that matters to your question.
paragraphs.locator: PDF section 2.4, physical pages 4 and 5

paragraphs.text: For a second example, ICNIRP’s DECT page distinguishes a base station from a portable handset or monitor near the body. Write each source arrangement separately in the worksheet, then ask which arrangement another report actually investigated. The application page also explains that much of its health discussion draws on mobile-phone and base-station research. That is a reason to inspect the underlying evidence, not to count the application page as an additional independent experiment.
paragraphs.locator: HTML: Characteristics of the application and its use; HF effects on the body and health implications

emf-reading-worksheet.title: A worked note without a risk score

paragraphs.text: Suppose the question is what a wearable measurement represents. The FOPH fact sheet distinguishes a device communicating through a phone from one using a mobile network directly. Enter that arrangement in the exposure box, together with the mode and position reported. Keep a separate question about whether your own device was tested. A shared product label does not document a matching model or operating condition.
paragraphs.locator: PDF introduction and section 1, physical pages 1 and 2

paragraphs.text: Under methods, record that FOPH describes measurements on selected devices using body-part phantoms. Under limitations, record its statement that this is not a market overview. The result is a source trail with a defined sample and test setting. It is not a calculation of an individual’s disease risk or a check that every device complies under every use. Use the original section to verify a number before repeating it.
paragraphs.locator: PDF section 2.4, physical pages 4 and 5

paragraphs.text: If your next source concerns a cordless phone, start a new note. ICNIRP separates the base station from a nearby handset or monitor, so one entry for all cordless exposure would conceal an important distinction. Write which part was studied and what the comparison describes. Ending with an unresolved match is useful: it identifies the information needed next without turning missing information into either reassurance or alarm.
paragraphs.locator: HTML: Characteristics of the application and its use

paragraphs.text: This source describes static magnetic fields as fields that do not vary in intensity or direction over time. It uses the Earth’s magnetic field, magnets and specialized industrial or medical equipment to illustrate that category. Those examples explain what the term means; they do not make all of the settings equivalent. In a reading note, preserve the actual source and setting before moving to a discussion of biological effects or protection.
paragraphs.locator: HTML: Characteristics of the field and its use

paragraphs.text: The protection section addresses several different situations. It links general static-field guidance, discusses working procedures for movement through strong fields, points to specific MRI patient recommendations and identifies implanted devices as a separate concern. These are distinct scopes within one overview. A sentence about general field exposure should therefore not be substituted for an MRI procedure assessment or an implant-specific assessment. Follow the linked original guidance for the situation actually being considered.
paragraphs.locator: HTML: Protection

paragraphs.text: Use the page to identify the field category and locate the relevant protection discussion. It is an official explanatory source, rather than a new clinical trial or an independent replication of every study it references. The selected passages summarized here do not establish a personal risk estimate, a complete equipment assessment or a certainty grade across all static-field outcomes. Reading the underlying guidance remains necessary when a technical condition matters to the question.
paragraphs.locator: HTML: Characteristics of the field and its use; Protection

icnirp-dect.title: Two parts of the same system

paragraphs.text: ICNIRP describes DECT as a technology used for cordless telephone systems and also in some baby monitors and industrial applications. Its exposure explanation distinguishes the local base station from a portable phone or monitor near the body. That distinction matters when reading a comparison: a measurement made around a base station and an assessment of a handset are different source arrangements, even though both are described as DECT.
paragraphs.locator: HTML: Characteristics of the application and its use

icnirp-dect.title: Trace the health discussion to its evidence

paragraphs.text: The application page states that much of the health discussion draws on mobile-phone and base-station literature. Treat that statement as a scope limit when using this record. An official application overview can explain how an organization interprets related evidence without becoming a new DECT-specific experiment. For an individual study claim, follow the underlying paper and retain the technology, population, exposure method and outcome that the paper actually investigated.
paragraphs.locator: HTML: HF effects on the body and health implications

icnirp-dect.title: Guidance is not a room measurement

paragraphs.text: The protection section discusses absorbed-energy limits and distinguishes whole-body exposure from the head exposure relevant to handset use. Its role is to explain the guidance framework, not to measure a reader’s equipment or reconstruct a room’s exposure. Keep the quantity and scenario beside any technical comparison. This record provides source-linked context with scientific and human review still pending; it does not supply a device-specific certificate or a new clinical verdict.
paragraphs.locator: HTML: Protection

paragraphs.text: The fact sheet describes trackers and smartwatches as devices with different possible communication arrangements. Some communicate through nearby devices using low-powered wireless technologies; some can connect directly to a mobile network. It also distinguishes a tracker’s functions from the additional communication functions of a smartwatch. When comparing sources, preserve the active radio and connection path. The category name alone does not establish that two reports tested the same arrangement.
paragraphs.locator: PDF introduction and section 1, physical pages 1 and 2

foph-wearables.title: Read how the measurements were made

paragraphs.text: Section 2.4 describes measurements of selected trackers and watches and explicitly says the work is not a market overview. It explains tests using phantoms representing exposed body parts, with operating modes, frequency bands, positions and contact conditions defined for the measurements. These details describe the test rather than optional background. A result should stay attached to them instead of being generalized to every device, position or activity.
paragraphs.locator: PDF section 2.4, physical pages 4 and 5

foph-wearables.title: Separate exposure from a health conclusion

paragraphs.text: The document discusses health evidence and exposure measurements in different sections. Its measurement setup does not follow people over time to measure a clinical outcome. A reading summary should therefore identify whether it is describing a tested exposure, the document’s guidance discussion or evidence about health. This source record keeps those contributions bounded. It does not add a market-wide ranking, an individual risk estimate or a formal evidence grade.
paragraphs.locator: PDF sections 2.1 and 2.4, physical pages 2 to 5

nci-emf-cancer.title: The field definition comes before the cancer question

paragraphs.text: NCI explains electric fields in relation to voltage and magnetic fields in relation to electric current. It then separates higher-frequency ionizing radiation from the lower-frequency field categories relevant to this fact sheet. Those distinctions help identify what a report measured. They do not replace the report’s exposure definition. Keep the quantity, source and study setting visible when moving from the physical explanation to a statement about a health outcome.
paragraphs.locator: HTML: What are electric and magnetic fields?

nci-emf-cancer.title: Use source examples without merging their evidence

paragraphs.text: The common-sources section places power lines, wiring and household appliances in the low-frequency discussion and wireless communication equipment in the radiofrequency discussion. These examples orient the reader; they are not a claim that every source has the same exposure pattern or cancer evidence. A report on a household appliance should retain its own measurement or use history, and a wireless-device study should retain its actual technology and population.
paragraphs.locator: HTML: What are common sources of non-ionizing EMFs?

nci-emf-cancer.title: Keep the outcome and uncertainty attached

paragraphs.text: The childhood-cancer discussion distinguishes power-line exposure, appliance use and other source settings, and describes uncertainty in interpreting the observational findings. A summary should preserve the specific diagnosis and exposure comparison instead of announcing a single conclusion for all EMFs. This fact sheet is a context source with references to underlying research. Counting its references is not equivalent to independently appraising each paper, and this record does not claim that such an appraisal is complete.
paragraphs.locator: HTML: What have studies shown about possible associations between non-ionizing EMFs and cancer in children?

paragraphs.text: UKHSA describes a home-area network linking meters and an in-home display, alongside a communication module that sends information to the utility company. The document says data are sent in short intermittent bursts. A source description should therefore identify which link and operating condition it concerns. A meter system is not fully described by a technology name alone, and a brief transmission measurement is different from a time-averaged exposure estimate.
paragraphs.locator: HTML: Radio waves and smart meters

ukhsa-smart-meters.title: Read each research phase by its purpose

paragraphs.text: The programme described here separates laboratory emission measurements, calculations of energy absorption in the body and measurements in a sample of homes. These are related exposure assessments with different settings. They are not three independent clinical trials measuring illness. Keep the tested device, position and measurement or modeling method beside the finding. A summary should preserve that distinction before relating the result to a different installation or health question.
paragraphs.locator: HTML: Exposures from smart meters

home.title: Three ways to read a source carefully

paragraphs.text: Start by identifying the exposure. NCI separates fields associated with electrical power systems from radiofrequency sources such as wireless communication equipment. That physical distinction helps you choose the relevant source pages before comparing outcomes. Keep the device, field quantity and setting together in your notes. A broad EMF label is useful for discovery, but it does not show that two studies examined the same exposure.
paragraphs.locator: HTML: What are electric and magnetic fields?; What are common sources of non-ionizing EMFs?

paragraphs.text: Next ask what was actually measured. UKHSA’s smart-meter explanation distinguishes laboratory emissions, modeled absorption in the body and exposure measurements in homes. Those approaches describe different parts of the exposure question. A measurement report can help characterize a setting without being a clinical trial. Use the source records to inspect the method and its limits before transferring a conclusion to a different device or outcome.
paragraphs.locator: HTML: Exposures from smart meters

paragraphs.text: Finally check the document’s date and purpose. The WHO EHS backgrounder linked here dates from December 2005. It recognizes that symptoms can be real and disabling while separating the symptom experience from its attribution to a particular exposure. That historical explanation is context, rather than an updated review of every current wireless technology. Our source records retain the document’s date and review limits so you can see what each source contributes.
paragraphs.locator: HTML: Backgrounder, December 2005; Conclusions

paragraphs.text: This backgrounder is dated December 2005 and describes its basis in earlier workshops and literature. Retain that date when citing its conclusions. It is not a new clinical experiment and does not represent a fresh search covering every later device or technology. The record is useful for understanding how the document defines the reported symptom problem, while later evidence requires its own source-specific assessment.
paragraphs.locator: HTML: Backgrounder, December 2005; introductory scope paragraphs

who-ehs.title: Separate symptoms from an explanation of their cause

paragraphs.text: WHO’s conclusions recognize that symptoms can be real, differ in severity and become disabling. The document distinguishes that experience from identifying an EMF cause or a single diagnostic condition. A faithful summary should retain both parts, rather than dismissing symptoms or treating the term EHS as a verified exposure diagnosis. This source record explains the historical document; it does not assess an individual’s symptoms or provide a personal treatment plan.
paragraphs.locator: HTML: Conclusions

icnirp-mri.title: An MRI system has several field components

paragraphs.text: ICNIRP describes MRI as combining a strong static magnetic field with low-frequency and high-frequency fields. Calling the system a magnet or labeling everything radiofrequency loses that distinction. In a reading note, identify which component and activity the source addresses. A statement about staff moving through a static field should not automatically become a conclusion about a patient’s radiofrequency exposure or about every part of the imaging procedure.
paragraphs.locator: HTML: Characteristics of the application and its use; Protection

icnirp-mri.title: Patient and staff questions have different scopes

paragraphs.text: The protection discussion separates medical exposure of patients from exposure of personnel working near MRI equipment. It explains that movement through a strong static field can be relevant to transient sensory effects in staff. A source summary should keep the person’s role and activity beside the field description. This overview helps locate those issues; it does not replace an assessment of a particular scan, workplace task or patient’s medical circumstances.
paragraphs.locator: HTML: Protection, patient and personnel paragraphs

foph-bluetooth.title: Name the variant and the task

paragraphs.text: The fact sheet distinguishes Bluetooth classic from Bluetooth Low Energy and describes applications including audio, computer peripherals, sensors and wearable connections. Those examples involve different tasks and connection arrangements. A comparison should name the device’s role and the activity being assessed instead of treating every Bluetooth label as the same exposure. The technical description is a starting point for matching a source to a question, rather than a product recommendation.
paragraphs.locator: PDF introduction, physical page 1; section 1.2, physical page 2

foph-bluetooth.title: An exposure comparison is not a clinical outcome

paragraphs.text: FOPH discusses head exposure during a phone call when using a Bluetooth headset compared with holding the phone at the head. That comparison concerns exposure in the specified arrangement. It does not by itself measure a health benefit from using a headset. The fact sheet also keeps its discussion of short-term exposure separate from uncertainty about long-term health effects. Retain that boundary instead of turning the comparison into a general clinical verdict.
paragraphs.locator: PDF highlighted assessment and headset tip, physical page 1

icnirp-lf.title: Electric and magnetic quantities are distinct

paragraphs.text: ICNIRP’s low-frequency explanation describes time-varying electric and magnetic fields and identifies electrical power generation, distribution and use as major sources. It gives the electric and magnetic components different quantities and units. A reading note should therefore record which component was measured before comparing numbers. An appliance-use description or a distance from a power line also needs its own exposure definition; it is not automatically a direct measurement of either field component.
paragraphs.locator: HTML: Frequency range and LF use

icnirp-lf.title: Keep the interaction and outcome questions separate

paragraphs.text: The source describes induced internal electric fields and stimulation of excitable tissues at sufficient exposure. It discusses longer-term observational health questions separately. These are different lines of evidence, so an explanation of an established interaction does not settle every chronic-outcome question. This record provides context for the framework. Any specific health claim still needs the relevant population, exposure measure, outcome and underlying research, with scientific appraisal and human review kept explicit.
paragraphs.locator: HTML: LF effects on the body and health implications; Protection

fda-microwave.title: Cooking, leakage and injury are different questions

paragraphs.text: The FDA explains that microwave energy absorbed by food becomes heat and does not make the food radioactive. Its page separately discusses radiation leakage, the oven door and interlocks, and injuries from hot food, containers or superheated water. A claim about one of those issues should name it. A burn during food handling is not automatically evidence of radiation leakage, and an oven-performance discussion is not a study of every household wireless exposure.
paragraphs.locator: HTML: Cooking with Microwaves; Microwave Oven Safety Standard; Have Radiation Injuries Resulted from Microwave Ovens?

fda-microwave.title: Retain the product and jurisdictional scope

paragraphs.text: The performance standard described by this source concerns microwave ovens under the US FDA framework. Keep that product scope beside any technical comparison rather than treating the page as one exposure threshold for all EMF outcomes. The original document also directs readers to manufacturer instructions and distinguishes proper operation from unusual damage or servicing situations. This record preserves those distinctions without inspecting a particular oven or asserting that an individual product meets the standard.
paragraphs.locator: HTML: Microwave Oven Safety Standard; Checking Ovens for Leakage and Other Radiation Safety Problems

paragraphs.text: The fact sheet distinguishes dedicated baby and parent units, network cameras, walkie-talkies and phone-based monitoring. It also describes voice activation and range-check signals as separate functions. Those details affect what the device is doing during an exposure measurement. Record which units transmit, the active function and the arrangement tested. The term baby monitor alone does not show that another report examined the same equipment or operating state.
paragraphs.locator: PDF opening device descriptions, physical page 1; section 1.1, physical page 3

foph-baby-monitors.title: Do not extend the stated scope to other features

paragraphs.text: FOPH states that the document covers audio and video monitoring and excludes advanced functions that monitor a baby’s bodily functions. Its exposure discussion concerns measured devices and specified conditions. That does not validate every additional feature, establish diagnostic accuracy or certify every current model. Keep the document’s exclusions with the summary, and follow the original source when a device-specific condition matters. This record remains an official-context reading with scientific and human review pending.
paragraphs.locator: PDF opening scope, physical page 1; Exposure to radiation, physical pages 1 and 2

hse-workplace.title: Read this as a workplace framework

paragraphs.text: HSE’s explanation separates sensory effects, direct health effects and indirect effects such as interference with implanted devices or attraction of metal objects. Those are different assessment questions within the workplace framework described by the document. Retain the worker, task and equipment context rather than applying one category to every setting. This source record explains a UK-specific official document; it is not a finding that every workplace shares the same exposure.
paragraphs.locator: HTML: EMF effects covered by the Regulations

hse-workplace.title: Identify the information used in an assessment

paragraphs.text: The document describes using equipment and emission information and considering the work actually performed, including workers at particular risk. It discusses measurements or calculations when existing information is insufficient. That is a process for evaluating a setting, rather than a new trial of a health intervention. A summary should distinguish the source’s regulatory scope from the evidence needed for a specific clinical claim. Current compliance and individual circumstances require their own authoritative assessment.
paragraphs.locator: HTML: What you must you do as an employer

foph-induction.title: Keep the pan and operating configuration visible

paragraphs.text: FOPH explains induction cooking through a magnetic field that produces currents and magnetization in the pan base. The pan does not capture the entire field. The fact sheet also describes the importance of pan size, placement, power and the person’s position when considering exposure. A comparison should preserve those conditions. The appliance name alone cannot tell you whether two measurements describe the same cooking setup.
paragraphs.locator: PDF opening explanation and recommendations, physical pages 1 and 2; section 1.2, physical pages 3 and 4

foph-induction.title: Measurements and pregnancy outcomes need different evidence

paragraphs.text: The source discusses field measurements and exposure-limit comparisons separately from the limited pregnancy-outcome literature it describes. A measurement in a particular cooking configuration is not itself a clinical outcome for a mother or baby. Retain that distinction and the source’s limits when reading a headline. This record does not add a universal distance rule, an individual risk calculation or a product ranking, and it does not promote the underlying literature to a completed scientific appraisal.
paragraphs.locator: PDF opening health discussion, physical page 1

paragraphs.text: The selected participants reported phone-related headache or discomfort and underwent an open exposure test before the blinded comparisons. The report found no demonstrated difference between the tested radiofrequency and sham conditions. That result concerns symptoms in this selected group under an acute protocol; it does not identify the medical cause of every headache.
paragraphs.locator: Saved publisher PDF web extraction, physical page 7, lines 649 to 662

paragraphs.text: The authors proposed negative expectations as an explanation. They also acknowledged that the study could not properly isolate a nocebo effect: symptoms during open radiofrequency exposure were an entry criterion, and there was no open sham comparison. Their interpretation should therefore remain separate from an experimentally demonstrated explanation for each participant.
paragraphs.locator: Saved publisher PDF web extraction, physical page 7, lines 611 to 627

icnirp-rf.title: Read the quantity before the limit

paragraphs.text: ICNIRP separates exposure outside the body from energy absorbed within it. Its basic restrictions concern absorbed quantities, while reference levels describe external fields and are derived using exposure assumptions. A field reading and a specific absorption rate therefore answer different measurement questions. The relevant frequency, exposed body region and averaging conditions belong with any comparison to the guidance.
paragraphs.locator: HTML Protection; Frequency range and use

paragraphs.text: The protection discussion addresses excessive whole-body and local heating. It describes conservative factors used when deriving restrictions from adverse-effect thresholds. This is an explanation of ICNIRP's framework, rather than a fresh study or a measurement of a particular reader's exposure. Using the framework for a device or workplace still requires the relevant exposure information and assessment conditions.
paragraphs.locator: HTML Protection; RF EMF effects on the body and health implications

paragraphs.text: The questionnaire recorded reported phone-use frequency and usual carrying position. Those categories are behavior measures, not a continuous record of transmission or absorbed dose. Semen testing at the examination supplies a different kind of measurement. Keeping the questionnaire exposure and laboratory outcome distinct helps explain why this cross-sectional comparison cannot by itself establish that radiofrequency exposure caused an individual result.
paragraphs.locator: Original PDF physical pages 3 and 8, questionnaire and statistical methods

paragraphs.text: The analysis considered several semen characteristics and different model comparisons. A reference threshold for a laboratory parameter is not an observed probability of conception. The authors discuss limitations including reported use and changes over the recruitment period. These distinctions constrain transfer from an association in sampled young men to a diagnosis of infertility or a claim about carrying a phone in a pocket.
paragraphs.locator: Original PDF physical pages 8 to 11, results and discussion

paragraphs.text: The abstract describes reuse of original individual records from several studies. It distinguishes estimated magnetic-field exposure from wire-code classifications, and reports that the wire-code associations varied across studies. These are related exposure approaches within the analysis, not interchangeable measurements or separate independent confirmations of the same result.
paragraphs.locator: Held Europe PMC core abstract, PMID 11055621, opening methods and wire-code results

paragraphs.text: The authors suggest that any appreciable association may be concentrated in relatively high and uncommon exposures, and call for better information on highly exposed populations. That bounded conclusion should travel with the higher-category finding. The abstract does not provide enough detail to clear the complete methods, tables or exact overlap with other pooled analyses. No new numerical estimate or causal conclusion is added here.
paragraphs.locator: Held Europe PMC core abstract, PMID 11055621, concluding sentences; abstract-only source scope

paragraphs.text: The FOPH fact sheet relates WLAN emissions to traffic and the network's transmission and reception characteristics. Its exposure summary distinguishes laboratory conditions from everyday measurements. A router's nominal output or a device's presence therefore does not, by itself, describe the exposure at a person's location. The sheet's interpretation is an agency assessment of the evidence it discusses, not a new certainty grade assigned by this site.
paragraphs.locator: PDF physical page 1, operating description and exposure/evidence summary

paragraphs.text: The additional-information section warns against inferring exposure from the number and displayed strength of nearby networks. It also describes the difficulty of measuring wireless-device emissions with ordinary handheld equipment. Read those measurement limits alongside the optional exposure-reduction suggestions. The fact sheet explicitly separates suggestions for personal preference from measures it considers necessary to prevent an established WLAN health risk.
paragraphs.locator: PDF physical pages 1 to 2, suggestions preamble and Additional information

paragraphs.text: HERMES assessed changes in verbal and figural memory tests in adolescents. Its exposure estimate combined reported device use, operator information for a subset and dose modeling. A modeled brain-dose estimate is not an assigned exposure or a continuous direct measurement within the brain. The outcome is performance on specified tests, rather than a diagnosis of neurological injury.
paragraphs.locator: Original PDF physical pages 1 to 4, Abstract and Materials and Methods

paragraphs.text: The paper explicitly compares this analysis with an earlier HERMES wave and describes changes in dose estimation. Shared programme participants mean the reports should not automatically count as independent replication. Operator information improves some use data but comes from a subset, while model uncertainty and differences between cognitive tests remain. Those qualifications matter when interpreting a more suggestive subgroup alongside the full-sample result.
paragraphs.locator: Original PDF physical page 11, Comparison with Previous Analysis and Brain Exposure

paragraphs.text: INTERPHONE compared interviews about earlier phone use among brain-tumour cases and controls. In its abstract, the authors discuss lower estimates for regular use alongside a higher glioma estimate in the greatest recalled call-time category. They identify implausible reported use in that category and possible participation bias in the overall comparisons. Neither pattern should be selected without the accompanying qualification.
paragraphs.locator: Held Europe PMC core abstract, PMID 20483835, Methods and Results

paragraphs.text: The abstract concludes that biases and error prevent a causal interpretation of the suggestion at the highest exposure levels. It calls for further investigation of long-term heavy use. This record retains its abstract-based scope: a bibliographic link or an available publisher address does not show that the full methods, tables and supplementary material were checked. The limitations apply to both reassuring and concerning readings of the result.
paragraphs.locator: Held Europe PMC core abstract, PMID 20483835, Conclusions; abstract-only source scope

cosmos.title: Calibration and follow-up answer different questions

paragraphs.text: COSMOS linked adult participants to cancer registries and calibrated reported call time using operator-recorded information. Registry follow-up improves ascertainment of the diagnosed outcomes; calibration addresses part of the exposure-measurement problem. These are separate strengths. Call time remains an estimate of behavior rather than an individual measurement of energy absorbed in brain tissue.
paragraphs.locator: Recovered published PDF physical pages 3 to 4, sections 2.2 and 2.3

paragraphs.text: The principal comparisons did not show an increased tumour-incidence pattern, while rare outcomes and the heaviest-use categories had more limited precision. The discussion also distinguishes historical handset technologies and changes in use. These limits prevent a universal conclusion about every wireless source, age or lifetime exposure. Further publications from the same cohort do not become independent cohorts merely because they address additional outcomes.
paragraphs.locator: Recovered published PDF physical pages 6 to 7, Discussion and conclusion; cohort description on page 3

foph-mobile.title: Connection quality and the meaning of SAR

paragraphs.text: FOPH explains that phone activity, connection quality and distance affect exposure. The maximum SAR rating describes specified test uses, including distinct head and body arrangements. It does not describe a person's continuous daily dose. A comparison of ratings should retain that test context rather than treat the larger label value as a measured dose during every call.
paragraphs.locator: PDF physical page 1, operating conditions and head/body SAR explanation

paragraphs.text: The fact sheet lists hands-free and headset options for people who wish to reduce exposure. It separately warns that shielding or harmonising products can impair the connection and increase transmission. These are statements about operation and exposure, not evidence from a trial proving that an accessory prevents illness. The distinction matters when reading product claims alongside the agency's discussion of remaining long-term uncertainty.
paragraphs.locator: PDF physical pages 1 to 2, exposure-reduction options and protective-product paragraph

guides.title: Choose a source that matches the question

paragraphs.text: For a guide about measurement, start by identifying the quantity. ICNIRP distinguishes absorbed-energy restrictions from external reference levels. Reading an outside field value as though it were an absorbed dose skips the relationship the guidance is designed to describe. Keep the frequency and exposure arrangement with the comparison.
paragraphs.locator: HTML Protection; Frequency range and use

paragraphs.text: For a guide about a household device, check the operating conditions. The FOPH WLAN sheet relates exposure to traffic, reception and distance, and warns that a list of visible networks is not an exposure measurement. An everyday scenario should therefore be matched to the source's measurement setting before its conclusion is reused.
paragraphs.locator: PDF physical pages 1 to 2, operating description and Additional information

paragraphs.text: For a guide about cancer, keep physical categories and health questions distinct. NCI separates ionizing from non-ionizing fields and discusses the designs used to investigate possible health effects. That orientation helps frame the question, while a specific study still needs its own population, exposure, outcome and limitations. None of these context sources supplies human scientific sign-off for this site's guides.
paragraphs.locator: HTML What are electric and magnetic fields?; Why are non-ionizing EMFs studied in relation to cancer?

E03-T05-R297.title: A review plan is not a completed result

paragraphs.text: The protocol separates experimental-mammal reproductive studies from experiments on human sperm outside the body. It also distinguishes pregnancy and developmental outcomes in exposed experimental mammals. These streams have different populations and endpoints. Their inclusion in a shared review plan does not make them studies of pregnancy or fertility outcomes in people.
paragraphs.locator: Native PMC XML abstract, Objectives and Study eligibility and criteria; sections s0030 and s0035

paragraphs.text: Risk-of-bias assessment, possible meta-analysis and certainty grading are described as planned methods. Whether data are sufficiently comparable determines the proposed synthesis approach. Those plans cannot supply a completed pooled effect or a certainty grade for this page. The recovered protocol supports reading the intended methods; completed reviews and amendments require their own version and source checks.
paragraphs.locator: Native PMC XML abstract, Study appraisal and synthesis method; Methods section s0035

wifi-pmid-17293700.title: Where the measurement was taken matters

paragraphs.text: The survey measured fields at varied locations and separately measured a laptop during large file transfers. The laptop setup was intended to characterize a nearby bystander in the antenna far field. The abstract explicitly says that exposure of a user in body contact with the antenna would require a different method. That exclusion belongs beside the exposure finding.
paragraphs.locator: Held indexed abstract, laptop file-transfer, far-field and excluded body-contact measurement sentences

paragraphs.text: The authors compared measured signal levels with the international limits used in the study and discussed low operating power and intermittent transmission. This is a historical measurement comparison under the sampled conditions. It does not measure a health outcome or supply a universal value for present-day homes. Full calibration, operating and uncertainty details remain outside this abstract-only reading.
paragraphs.locator: Held indexed abstract, final measurement-limit and technical-factor sentences; abstract-only access scope

paragraphs.text: WLAN data transmissions occur in bursts. The authors therefore distinguish an assumption of continuous activity from the duty cycles observed for particular applications and environments. A transfer task and light browsing do not necessarily occupy the channel for the same share of time. That distinction changes how a transmission-level measurement is used to describe an average exposure.
paragraphs.locator: Held indexed abstract, opening time-averaging and application-specific duty-cycle sentences

paragraphs.text: The abstract reports higher duty cycles at lower physical data rates and explains why a poorer connection need not imply lower possible exposure. Its observed summaries, application scenarios and theoretical bounds should remain separate. None is an observed clinical effect or a complete individual absorbed dose. The full sampling and calculation methods remain inaccessible in this reading.
paragraphs.locator: Held indexed abstract, theoretical-upper-limit, lower-data-rate and application-comparison sentences; abstract-only scope

paragraphs.text: The report describes an exposure system assessed using field measurements and anatomical modeling, followed by experiments on waking EEG and sustained attention. The EEG task involved watching a documentary; the vigilance task measured reaction time. These are specified short-term endpoints. They should not be relabeled as overnight sleep, a clinical neurological diagnosis or every aspect of cognition.
paragraphs.locator: Held indexed abstract, exposure-system/dosimetry description and experimental-task sentences

paragraphs.text: The authors report no measurable effect on the tested EEG spectral power or vigilance reaction time. The exposure-model description also uses a normalization condition, which should not be confused with a complete account of delivered dose in the experiments. Full methods are needed to assess control conditions, masking, participant flow and precision. Those unresolved inputs remain visible rather than being treated as evidence of equivalence.
paragraphs.locator: Held indexed abstract, normalized SAR description, experiment descriptions and concluding findings; abstract-only scope

wifi-pmid-22004929.title: A spatial pattern is not a health outcome

paragraphs.text: The laboratory study assessed Wi-Fi devices used in schools. It describes directional emission patterns for laptops and a different pattern for access points. A reading therefore needs the direction and measurement geometry, not only the device label. An emission pattern around equipment is different from a measurement of energy absorbed within a particular person.
paragraphs.locator: Held indexed abstract, objective and laptop/access-point radiation-pattern sentences

paragraphs.text: The abstract uses different integration geometries for laptop and access-point radiated power and separately discusses power density at measurement distances. These quantities should not be merged into a single dose or a child-health result. The comparison with a reference level applies to the reported setup. Complete operating conditions, calibration and uncertainty cannot be appraised from the accessible abstract alone.
paragraphs.locator: Held indexed abstract, spherical/hemispherical integration and final power-density/reference-level sentences; abstract-only scope

wifi-pmid-21856328.title: Observed duty factors and derived examples

paragraphs.text: The school study used packet capture and transmit-time information to assess intermittent Wi-Fi activity during classroom lessons. Its sampled laptop and access-point duty factors describe network use during those observations. A duty factor is part of time averaging; it is not itself a tissue dose or a diagnosis. The limited school sample remains part of the result.
paragraphs.locator: Held indexed abstract, time-averaging introduction and packet-capture/transmit-time methods

paragraphs.text: The final exposure examples apply the observed duty factors to previously published project results. The child-model SAR example is therefore a calculation using that project relationship, not a newly observed biological outcome in children. Related laboratory and classroom reports can provide complementary information without becoming independent health studies. Full capture validation, lesson sampling and model details remain unresolved here.
paragraphs.locator: Held indexed abstract, final sentences applying duty factors to prior project results; abstract-only scope

wifi-pmid-32408065.title: Show sleep and EEG findings together

paragraphs.text: The experiment compared overnight Wi-Fi and sham exposure in healthy young men, using both sleep questionnaires and polysomnography. The reported lack of a statistically significant change in subjective sleep or sleep macrostructure should be shown alongside the reduction in alpha-band EEG power during NREM sleep. They concern different endpoints within the same experiment.
paragraphs.locator: Held indexed abstract, Methods and Results

paragraphs.text: The authors did not interpret the EEG change as a sleep-disturbing effect in this protocol. A physiological difference alone is not a diagnosis of a sleep disorder, while a nonsignificant sleep comparison does not establish every possible effect is absent. Applicability remains bounded to the acute laboratory conditions and selected participants. Full effect estimates, analysis details, supplements and harms assessment are still needed for scientific appraisal.
paragraphs.locator: Held indexed abstract, Discussion and participant/experimental-setting description; abstract-only scope

paragraphs.text: This paper calculates fields around a charging-station transformer using selected source geometries and anatomical models. The modeled adult and child are not recruited participants, and internal field estimates are not observed clinical outcomes. Distance and shielding patterns describe the chosen computational arrangement. They cannot alone establish the exposure around every charger or vehicle.
paragraphs.locator: Held original PDF physical pages 3 to 10, Model Construction and simulation results

paragraphs.text: The limitations acknowledge that the model did not combine all charging-system sources and had not been validated with field measurements. The source also contains inconsistent percentage and category wording, so no compliance percentage is released here. Independent validation and broader source and anatomical configurations remain separate tasks. The engineering result should retain those limits when it is used in a health discussion.
paragraphs.locator: Held original PDF physical pages 19 to 21, summaries, Conclusions and limitations; source-specific numerical estimates withheld

outcomes.title: Match the endpoint to the evidence

paragraphs.text: A device measurement describes exposure conditions. The school Wi-Fi laboratory report, for example, measures emissions and spatial patterns rather than disease, symptoms or fertility. It can inform how a health question is framed without becoming a health-outcome experiment.
paragraphs.locator: Held indexed abstract, objective and measurement descriptions

paragraphs.text: A physiological measurement and a reported symptom also need separate labels. The overnight Wi-Fi experiment reports sleep outcomes alongside an EEG difference. Keeping both visible avoids treating every physiological change as a diagnosed disorder or every nonsignificant symptom comparison as proof of universal safety.
paragraphs.locator: Held indexed abstract, Results and Discussion

paragraphs.text: A simulation adds another kind of evidence. The electric-vehicle charging paper models fields in selected geometries and acknowledges missing field validation and incomplete source combinations. Those calculations are useful for understanding the model, while human health outcomes require their own evidence. Human scientific review for this reading edition remains pending.
paragraphs.locator: Held original PDF physical pages 3 to 10 and 21, model construction and limitations

E02-T03-R091.title: A masked acute comparison and its limits

paragraphs.text: The experiment compared real and sham WCDMA exposure near the head in selected adults with and without self-attributed sensitivity. It recorded symptoms, autonomic measures and exposure belief. The reported absence of significant active-versus-sham differences concerns this short-term protocol. It is not a diagnosis of every participant's symptoms or a test of all chronic exposures.
paragraphs.locator: Held original PDF physical pages 2 to 6, Subjects, procedure, analysis and results

paragraphs.text: A greater tendency to believe exposure was present appeared in the sensitive group during both conditions. That pattern is different from reliably identifying the real signal. The authors' expectation-based interpretation should remain distinct from a randomized test of expectation itself. Volunteer selection, exclusions and repeated responses also constrain inference; full scientific and human appraisal remain pending.
paragraphs.locator: Held original PDF physical pages 5 to 7, exposure-belief results and Discussion

wifi-pmid-32104921.title: A facility report and the experiment it supports

paragraphs.text: This report describes how a controlled head-exposure system delivers WLAN signals for blinded sleep experiments. Directional antennas, computer control and recorded forward and reverse power are engineering features of that setup. They help specify the exposure conditions; they do not, by themselves, report a sleep or other health outcome.
paragraphs.locator: Held indexed abstract, exposure-system design, signal-pattern and quality-control sentences

paragraphs.text: The abstract distinguishes absorption averaged over brain regions from peak spatial absorption and describes variation with head position. Those quantities should not be exchanged simply because each is called SAR. The report belongs with the sleep project as a methods companion, rather than an independent health trial. Full validation and uncertainty methods remain inaccessible in this abstract-only reading.
paragraphs.locator: Held indexed abstract, regional absorption, head-position variation and peak spatial SAR sentences; abstract-only scope

paragraphs.text: The study compares self-reported tinnitus and electromagnetic-sensitivity status in a selected group and controls. It reports more tinnitus in respondents describing sensitivity, while its phone-use measure did not show an association with tinnitus. These are different comparisons. Coexistence of the reported symptoms is not a measurement demonstrating that an electromagnetic field caused them.
paragraphs.locator: Original PDF physical page 4, Discussion

paragraphs.text: The cross-sectional design does not establish which condition preceded the other. Tinnitus reporting, response selection and differences in sleep or psychological measures also matter to interpretation. The proposed shared mechanism remains an explanation to investigate, rather than a demonstrated pathway. Related reports from the same research sample should not automatically count as independent replication.
paragraphs.locator: Original PDF physical pages 4 to 5, Discussion, limitations and Conclusion

E04-T07-R230.title: Occupational assignment is a group estimate

paragraphs.text: Job histories were mapped to occupational magnetic-field estimates using a job-exposure matrix. This assigns exposure information by occupation rather than measuring each worker at every task or workstation. Cumulative, average and highest-job metrics describe different summaries of that assignment. Within-job variation remains a limitation even when the work history itself is detailed.
paragraphs.locator: Original PDF physical pages 2 to 3, Materials and Methods

paragraphs.text: The study did not show a coherent overall meningioma association across its exposure metrics and time windows. An isolated intermediate-category elevation remains visible, so a narrative statement that every category was nonsignificant would be too absolute. These historical, outcome-specific comparisons do not establish a workplace safety threshold. Overlap with related case-control reports also needs attention before counting independent confirmation.
paragraphs.locator: Original PDF physical pages 4 to 5, Tables, Discussion and Conclusion

E01-T01-R126.title: Comparison groups and patterns across analyses

paragraphs.text: The paper reconstructs mobile and cordless phone histories using questionnaires in a case-control sample. Its reference definition matters because relatively few respondents were entirely unexposed and many used several phone technologies. Reported call histories are therefore behavior-based exposure measures, rather than individual measurements of absorbed dose.
paragraphs.locator: Original PDF physical pages 2 to 3, Methods; pages 8 to 9, Discussion and Conclusions

paragraphs.text: The authors describe no conclusive overall meningioma association while retaining a signal in the highest cumulative-use group. A consistent pattern across latency and laterality comparisons was absent, and some technology estimates were sparse. The finding should stay specific to the tumour and sampled history. Shared controls or research series do not become independent evidence merely because the exposure analysis or paper title changes.
paragraphs.locator: Original PDF physical pages 6 to 9, Results, Discussion and Conclusions

E03-T06-R139.title: Reported appliance use and delivery outcomes

paragraphs.text: Participants reported the type and use of induction cooker and later reported delivery outcomes through an internet research panel. Those answers do not measure personal magnetic-field dose. Missing information about distance, operating power and utensils limits how a reported use category can be translated into a physical exposure. The delivery endpoint should remain distinct from the appliance-use description.
paragraphs.locator: Original PDF physical pages 2 to 4, methods and exposure/outcome definitions; page 7, limitations

paragraphs.text: The paper discusses weak associations in selected use categories without a consistent birth-weight association. Substantial nonresponse, self-reported outcomes and selection of positive comparisons for adjusted analysis constrain causal interpretation. The authors considered alternative explanations rather than concluding that cooker use causes pregnancy harm. Changing an appliance was not tested as a preventive intervention, and no clinical recommendation follows from these comparisons alone.
paragraphs.locator: Original PDF physical page 6, Table and Discussion; page 7, limitations and Conclusion

sources.title: Match the source to the physical quantity

paragraphs.text: The same everyday word, field, can refer to different physical quantities. NCI distinguishes electric from magnetic fields and describes ionizing and non-ionizing categories. Start with the device and field type before comparing findings from a different source. A source category is a way to frame the question, not a health-effect estimate.
paragraphs.locator: Held official HTML, What are electric and magnetic fields?; What are common sources of non-ionizing EMFs?

paragraphs.text: ICNIRP distinguishes external reference levels from restrictions expressed through absorbed quantities. A field measurement around equipment and an estimate of absorption in tissue therefore answer different questions. Frequency, exposure arrangement and averaging conditions belong with a comparison to that framework.
paragraphs.locator: Held official HTML, Frequency range and use; Protection

paragraphs.text: For a mobile phone, FOPH explains that activity, connection quality and distance affect exposure. A maximum SAR rating describes specified test arrangements rather than a continuous personal daily dose. Those operating conditions help interpret the source pages without turning a device specification into a diagnosis or an individual prediction. Human scientific review of this reading edition remains pending.
paragraphs.locator: Held original PDF physical page 1, operating conditions and head/body SAR explanation

E03-T05-R354.title: Cell culture findings and their clinical boundary

paragraphs.text: The report examines cultured mouse Leydig cells under selected handset and generator exposure arrangements. Its metabolic, hormone and fluorescence assays describe responses in that culture system. Selected changes appear alongside a nonsignificant viability contrast, and oxidation-sensitive fluorescence did not change consistently across the arrangements. A summary should preserve that mixed endpoint pattern rather than describing every measured response as changed.
paragraphs.locator: Main PDF physical pages 5 to 9, Results and Figures

paragraphs.text: Cultured cells are not recruited participants, and a hormone assay is not a test of conception or reproductive success. The experimental methods identify the cell line and exposure arrangements; those details bound the finding to the tested system. The paper does not establish a clinical infertility outcome in people. The selected passages shown here still require complete scientific appraisal, numerical reconciliation and human review.
paragraphs.locator: Main PDF physical pages 2 to 5, cell culture and exposure methods; pages 9 to 12, Discussion and Conclusion

E03-T05-R320.title: Reproductive indicators and conflicting source statements

paragraphs.text: This experiment reports testicular, hormone and sperm measurements in exposed male rats. Selected differences coexist with nonsignificant comparisons, so the paper should not be summarized as showing a uniform change in every fertility indicator. The measured indicators also differ from successful mating, conception or offspring outcomes. The study did not directly test a clinical infertility diagnosis in people.
paragraphs.locator: Main PDF physical pages 3 to 6, Results, Tables and histology figure

paragraphs.text: Exposure units, the direction of an endpoint change and statements about significance are not consistent across the source. Those discrepancies remain unresolved rather than being repaired by choosing a convenient value or sentence. Group size, shared cage conditions and incomplete dosimetry also constrain interpretation. No numerical estimate is released here, and the selected qualitative passages do not replace a complete appraisal or human scientific review.
paragraphs.locator: Main PDF physical pages 2 to 3 and 5 to 7, Methods, Discussion and Conclusion

E02-T03-R207.title: Tested exposure and perceived exposure are different comparisons

paragraphs.text: The masked comparison concerns immediate symptoms and physiological measures during a specified multiband exposure and sham arrangement. Under those tested conditions, the actual-exposure comparison did not identify an adverse pattern. Initially correct exposure guesses did not persist when testing was repeated. These observations describe the protocol and selected participants rather than every possible signal, symptom or duration of exposure.
paragraphs.locator: Main PDF physical pages 4 to 6, analysis and Results

paragraphs.text: Associations with believing that exposure occurred need separate interpretation because perceived exposure was not randomly assigned. Such associations do not isolate a causal expectation mechanism. Sparse symptom observations and unreconciled paired counts also limit a strong equivalence claim. The paper should therefore retain both the actual-exposure comparison and the uncertainty around perception associations, without turning either into a universal diagnosis or a clinical recommendation.
paragraphs.locator: Main PDF physical pages 5 to 8, source tables, Discussion and limitations

E03-T05-R270.title: Animal surrogates and the explanation of a response

paragraphs.text: The rat experiment reports selected sperm, hormone and apoptosis-related differences alongside unchanged measures. Sperm abnormality, gross morphology and several Sertoli-cell measures should remain visible as nonsignificant findings. This mixture is more specific than a claim that all reproductive functions were impaired. The measured sperm and tissue indicators are also distinct from mating, conception and offspring outcomes.
paragraphs.locator: Main PDF physical pages 6 to 9, Results and Figures

paragraphs.text: The abstract and detailed morphology results differ, so the narrative retains that source conflict. Local thermal characterization is incomplete, and a continuous-wave comparison is absent. The design therefore does not establish that a response is uniquely due to pulsing or that it has a nonthermal mechanism. These animal surrogate observations do not establish human infertility, and scientific, numerical and human review remain pending.
paragraphs.locator: Main PDF physical pages 2 to 5 and 9 to 10, Methods and Discussion

E01-T01-R127.title: A pooled association and its comparison groups

paragraphs.text: The pooled case-control report combines acoustic-neuroma samples from different diagnosis periods and reconstructs mobile and cordless phone histories by questionnaire. It reports higher odds with wireless-phone use, particularly in longer-latency categories. The authors also note sparse comparisons for some technologies and that many participants used several phone types. These features matter when interpreting a technology-specific estimate as though it represented a separate, precisely measured exposure.
paragraphs.locator: Original PDF physical page 6, Discussion, Main findings and Strengths and limitations

paragraphs.text: Pooling adds information from the earlier sample; it does not create an independent replication of that sample. Hearing loss can also alter the ear used for calls, which complicates a comparison between tumour side and recalled phone side. The observed association remains specific to the sampled histories and outcome. It does not, by itself, isolate a causal mechanism or establish the risk for every phone technology and use pattern.
paragraphs.locator: Original PDF physical pages 6 to 7, Discussion and side-of-use interpretation

paragraphs.text: The study followed pregnancies while measuring magnetic fields at residential locations. Front-door average values and maximum alley values describe different aspects of those locations, and they did not give the same miscarriage association. A summary should retain that metric-dependent pattern. Selecting only the maximum-based result would hide the contrast with the front-door measure and the authors' more cautious overall interpretation.
paragraphs.locator: Original PDF physical page 5, Tables and Discussion; page 6, Conclusion

paragraphs.text: Participants did not wear personal dosimeters, and daily activities were not recorded. A reading outside a home therefore cannot reconstruct where someone spent time or their cumulative personal exposure. Confounding and the difference between a location measurement and an individual exposure remain relevant even in a prospective cohort. The report does not establish a general causal magnetic-field relationship or a preventive intervention for pregnancy.
paragraphs.locator: Original PDF physical pages 5 to 6, Discussion and Conclusion

E02-T03-R147.title: Different analyses and a mixed symptom pattern

paragraphs.text: The cohort estimates ambient exposure from fixed transmitters at home and school rather than measuring each adolescent's absorbed dose. That question differs from exposure to a phone used close to the body. Cross-sectional, follow-up and exposure-change analyses also ask different temporal questions, so their results should not be treated as interchangeable measurements of a single health effect.
paragraphs.locator: Original PDF physical pages 2 to 3, propagation-model methods; pages 6 to 7, interpretation

paragraphs.text: The symptom pattern is mixed: some cohort comparisons indicate more tiredness or concentration difficulty, while the change analyses include inverse associations and the cross-sectional comparisons do not show an overall association. The authors call for confirmation in light of the many analyses. Keeping positive, null and inverse findings visible avoids replacing this pattern with an absolute claim of either harm or no effect. Related HERMES reports also need an overlap check before counting independent confirmation.
paragraphs.locator: Original PDF physical pages 6 to 8, Table, Discussion and Conclusions

E03-T06-R149.title: A listed phone rating is not a measured fetal dose

paragraphs.text: Mothers recalled phone use, and the investigators assigned a SAR value from the reported phone brand and model. The listed rating and reported use time are different exposure proxies. Neither directly measures the energy absorbed by the mother or fetus during ordinary use. The hospital sample and exclusions also define which pregnancies the comparison can describe, rather than all phone users.
paragraphs.locator: Original PDF physical pages 2 to 3, Material and Methods and Results

paragraphs.text: The report found a phone-rating association with small-for-gestational-age birth while reported daily use time did not show the same pattern. Its receiver-operating-characteristic cutoff was derived within this selected dataset. Without independent validation or an adjusted causal comparison, that cutoff is not an established safety boundary or a tool for predicting an individual pregnancy. The source-specific covariate-table inconsistency remains unresolved, and numerical estimates are withheld pending review.
paragraphs.locator: Original PDF physical pages 3 to 5, Results, tables, Discussion and Conclusion

E06-T11-R168.title: Workplace maxima are a screening perspective

paragraphs.text: This review assembles published workplace measurements and accident reports rather than following a new cohort for disease. It emphasizes reported high values to identify settings where occupational action levels may be exceeded. Industrial dielectric heating, work near transmitters and maintenance scenarios therefore need their own context. A maximum selected from a publication is not automatically a worker's typical personal exposure.
paragraphs.locator: Original PDF physical pages 9 to 11, Discussion and limitations

paragraphs.text: The exposure comparison depends on averaging conditions, operating cycles, the relevant field quantity and whether several sources contribute. Measurements selected for high-exposure scenarios do not describe the prevalence of those conditions throughout an industry. They also do not estimate long-term disease incidence. The review's maintenance and accident examples should remain distinct from ordinary use of intact household equipment, and underlying reports require deduplication before being counted as independent evidence.
paragraphs.locator: Original PDF physical pages 10 to 11, Discussion, frequency components and representativeness limits

E01-T01-R022.title: Overall use and recalled side of use

paragraphs.text: The North European case-control analysis did not find an overall increase for regular mobile-phone use in its observed history. A same-side finding in longer use remains part of the result, rather than being erased by that overall summary. Those comparisons use reported call histories and side of use; they are not direct measurements of absorbed energy or a complete test of lifetime exposure.
paragraphs.locator: Original PDF physical pages 5 to 6, Discussion and summary

paragraphs.text: Tumour-related hearing loss can lead someone to change ears before diagnosis, while remembering use after diagnosis can introduce a different bias. The paper discusses these competing problems when interpreting laterality. An apparent same-side association therefore needs more than a simple causal reading. This report also contains the earlier Swedish component and belongs to INTERPHONE, so those related reports should not be counted again as independent cohorts.
paragraphs.locator: Original PDF physical pages 5 to 6, Discussion of hearing loss, recall and related reports

E04-T08-R052.title: Task changes and reported call behavior

paragraphs.text: The longitudinal child study compares changes in reported mobile and cordless voice calls with changes in cognitive tasks. Response time, errors and interference ratios describe different task outcomes. The isolated changes do not all point in the same direction, and the authors describe limited evidence for a consistent association. Combining them into a single claim of better or worse cognition would lose that distinction.
paragraphs.locator: Original PDF physical pages 7 to 8, Table and Discussion/Conclusions

paragraphs.text: Reported call counts are behavior proxies, and parent and child reports differed. Low use, dropout, short follow-up and many comparisons limit interpretation, while transformed task scales require care before describing clinical importance. Earlier cross-sectional ExPOSURE reports come from the same programme rather than an independent replication. These comparisons do not isolate absorbed RF dose from other correlates of phone use or establish a clinical developmental outcome.
paragraphs.locator: Original PDF physical pages 2 to 3, Methods; pages 7 to 8, Discussion and limitations

E02-T03-R222.title: Resting brain spectra and multiple comparisons

paragraphs.text: The experiment compares a specified laboratory exposure with sham during resting waking EEG recordings. A signal occupying a band used by mobile networks does not reproduce every deployed waveform, traffic pattern or near-head use condition. EEG spectral power is a physiological measurement, rather than a direct test of cognition, a sleep diagnosis or a clinical disease outcome.
paragraphs.locator: Main PDF physical pages 2 to 6, design, exposure system, EEG processing and Statistics

paragraphs.text: Isolated nominal electrode differences did not survive the reported cluster-based correction. That distinction matters when many bands, sensors, time periods and eye conditions are compared. The overall nonsignificant pattern should not be converted into proof that every possible exposure has no effect. The protocol is acute, and complete corrected-output reproducibility, scientific appraisal and human review remain pending.
paragraphs.locator: Main PDF physical pages 6 and 14 to 16, analysis, Discussion and Conclusions

E03-T06-R054.title: Earlier outcome recording and later exposure recall

paragraphs.text: This birth-cohort analysis uses early maternal reports of motor and cognitive/language milestones. The later questionnaire asked mothers to remember phone use during pregnancy. A cohort framework therefore does not make the exposure recollection a prospectively measured dose. Recalled calling behavior and carrying location also do not directly measure absorbed energy reaching the fetus.
paragraphs.locator: Main PDF physical pages 3 to 4, printed pages 342 to 343, Methods

paragraphs.text: The report found no coherent overall adverse association or use-pattern gradient in these early milestones. Isolated inverse item associations do not establish developmental benefit. Selection, missing outcomes and questionnaire screening limits remain, and numerical reporting discrepancies have not been resolved. Related later-behavior reports from the same cohort concern different endpoints and do not become independent birth-cohort replications. These findings do not establish universal prenatal safety.
paragraphs.locator: Main PDF physical pages 5 to 8, printed pages 344 to 347, Results, Tables and Discussion

E05-T09-R435.title: Cell assays, chemical challenge and clinical inference

paragraphs.text: The cultured neuroblastoma cells were compared under magnetic-field and sham conditions, with and without a menadione challenge. The report found no significant difference in comet-assay DNA damage or repair, or cytosolic superoxide.
